skills.name: x-mute-workflow
skills.description: Use when scanning X mentions for mute candidates or muting approved handles in the browser.
skills.content:
---
name: x-mute-workflow
description: >-
  Use when scanning X mentions for mute candidates or muting approved handles in
  the browser.
---
Use this when scanning X mentions for mute candidates or muting approved handles.

## Read mentions
1. Confirm the X connector. Check usage credits first. Stop cleanly on needsAuth or empty credits.
2. Resolve the authenticated user, then pull recent mentions (about last 24–36 hours).
3. Classify each mention: mute-worthy (insult, condescension, spam/scam/crypto shill, clear hostility) vs keep (questions, thanks, banter, normal disagreement, collaborators).
4. Show the user a short list: @handle, one-line reason with quote gist, link. Separate borderline. If empty: "Mute candidates: none."

## Approve then mute
5. Wait for explicit approval of specific handles. Do not mute from a vague "clean it up."
6. The X connector has no mute tool. For each approved handle: open https://x.com/{handle} in the signed-in browser, open More (⋯), Mute, confirm if prompted, close that profile, next.
7. Report muted / already muted / failed with a local timestamp. Never unmute, block, follow, unfollow, reply, or post as part of this job.

## Do not
- Auto-mute without approval
- Invent handles or quote text you did not see
- Require a vault, Dropbox, or third-party log unless the user asks for one

routines.name: Daily mute candidates
routines.description: Every morning, scan recent X mentions and surface mute candidates for user approval.
routines.content:
You scan the user's own X mentions for mute candidates. Use their local timezone for dates.

On each run:
1. Confirm the X connector is available. Check usage credits before expensive calls. Prefer mentions for the authenticated user (look up tools each run; do not assume a frozen schema).
2. Pull mentions since the previous window (about the last 24–36 hours).
3. Flag replies that are insulting, condescending, spam/scam/crypto shill, or clearly hostile. Skip normal disagreement, questions, thanks, collaborators, and banter.
4. Send a short briefing to the user: mute candidates with handle, one-line why (quote gist), and link. Mark borderline separately. If none, say "Mute candidates: none."
5. Do NOT mute, block, or open profiles to mute until the user explicitly approves specific handles.
6. After approval in chat, mute by opening each approved profile in the signed-in browser (More → Mute → confirm), one at a time, then close that profile. Report muted / already muted / failed. If login or {slack_channel_id} blocks you, stop and ask the user to sign in on this computer.

Never invent metrics or handles. Never mute anyone not on the approved list for that run.

Fires on:
- cron `3 8 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
- Slack channel id
